How it works

One transformer, from geometry to field

KuberNet ingests raw boundary geometry — a surface point cloud with normals — plus physics conditioning, and predicts (U, T, p) at any query point. No analytic signed-distance field is required, so it applies to arbitrary CAD.

Results

State of the art, without domain adaptation

On the public SIMSHIFT heatsink split (train fin counts 5–8 → test 10–12), Kuber leads on temperature — with none of the unsupervised domain adaptation every published baseline uses. Every number is measured and reproducible.

One model, two device classes

Heatsinks and cold plates from one set of weights

Distinguished only by a device flag and fluid/BC conditioning, a single model spans a buoyancy-driven heatsink in air and a forced-liquid cold plate. Held-out cold plates 3.11 K, heatsinks 5.13 K on our corpus (not comparable to the SIMSHIFT numbers).

Dataset

A self-generated OpenFOAM corpus

Parametric geometry → OpenFOAM buoyantSimpleFoam → per-node fields, resumable and convergence-gated. Zero cases from SIMSHIFT or any licensed source.
